explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/813: h(n) is minimal such that every graph on n vertices in which every 7 vertices contain a triangle has a clique on at least h(n) vertices; do there exist c₁, c₂ > 0 with n^{1/3+c₁} ≪ h(n) ≪ n^{1/2−c₂}? In Lean h n is the infimum of cliqueNum over graphs on Fin n satisfying EverySevenHasTriangle (every 7-set contains a 3-clique), which is exactly the guaranteed clique size (test: h 7 = 3). The statement ∃ c₁ > 0, ∃ c₂ > 0, n^{1/3+c₁} =O[atTop] h ∧ h =O[atTop] n^{1/2−c₂} matches the Vinogradov notation. Faithful.
